messages.subject: newbie question: plotting epoch timestamps
parts:
I dabble a bit with ggplot2 and R, and after searching around in vain
I'm still completely stumped on how to get ggplot2 to understand epoch
timestamps.

For example, how would I read in the following datafile and plot it so
it understands that timestamp is the date/time?

---datafile---
timestamp value
1306520201 110
1306523801 110
1306527408 110
1306531010 110
1306534614 110
1306779688 111
1306783289 111
1306786896 111
1306790496 111
1306797725 111
---datafile---

Here is my code to plot without understanding date/time:

mydata = read.table(file('datafile'),header=TRUE,sep=" ")
qplot(timestamp,value,data=mydata,geom="line")

Thanks for the help!

messages.author: 0c39e60ddb38622b
messages.subject: Re: newbie question: plotting epoch timestamps
parts:
Hi:

This might be a little cleaner visually, but I'm also using the
example to point out another one of the upcoming changes in 0.9.0:

## 0.8.9:

qplot(Datetime,value,data=df,geom="line") +
scale_x_datetime(format = '%b %d\n%H:%M')

## 0.9.0:
qplot(Datetime,value,data=df,geom="line") +
scale_x_datetime(labels = date_format('%b %d\n%H:%M'))

This is one example of how labels (and breaks) will be able to take
functions as arguments. The functions used for labels in 0.9.0 end in
_format() while the functions used to define breaks end in _breaks().

Dennis
